extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news managers, journalism students, media scholars, and educators interested in racial representation in local TV news
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing how and why local television newscasts cover (or fail to cover) people of color, including newsroom decision-making, organizational structures, and the social effects of coverage. The rubric covers content selection, managerial influence, access, geography/history factors, and qualitative/ethnographic methodology for study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of local news
rubrics_metrics.description: If the purpose of local news is to cover individual communities and to present issues of interest and concern to local audiences...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a newscast actually covers community-specific issues and interests rather than generic or centrally determined content. Look for stories that reflect local concerns, diversity of community voices, and relevance to varied audience segments. Anti-patterns: primarily syndicated or homogeneous items that ignore local minority communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity of local newscasts across markets
rubrics_metrics.description: Why are local newscasts so similar in markets around the country?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess homogeneity: examine story selection, formats, pacing, and beats to see whether stations replicate a nationalized template instead of tailoring coverage to their distinct local populations. Consider whether sameness reduces meaningful coverage of local minority communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningfulness of coverage of people of color
rubrics_metrics.description: Local television news coverage of people of color does not occur in more meaningful ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure depth, frequency, context, and framing of stories about people of color. Distinguish token or sensational coverage from substantive reporting that addresses structural issues, community voices, and long-term context. Examples: token human-interest pieces vs. investigative or community-impact reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptions of racism and ethnicity among news workers
rubrics_metrics.description: Heider examines the perceptions of racism and ethnicity [among newsroom staff].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how journalists' and managers' beliefs about race and ethnicity shape beats, sourcing, story selection, and framing. Look for explicit or implicit assumptions that lead to excluding or marginalizing minority communities. Include interviews/observations of newsroom attitudes when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: "White" news vs. on-air diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: "White" news (content determined by white managers) being delivered by non-white news anchors, thus giving the appearance of "non-white" news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between diversity of on-air personnel and diversity of editorial control and content. Assess who makes editorial decisions versus who appears on camera. Anti-pattern: diverse on-air faces masking homogeneous editorial agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of coverage on viewers' perceptions of minority neighbors
rubrics_metrics.description: How coverage of minorities influences viewers' perceptions of their minority neighbors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the social effects of news portrayals: whether reporting reinforces stereotypes, shapes fear or misunderstanding, or contributes to civic inclusion/exclusion. Use audience research or plausible inference from story framing and prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incognizant racism (theoretical concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: Heider sets forth a new theoretical concept--incognizant racism--as a way of explaining how news workers consistently ignore news in significant portions of the communities they cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this concept to diagnose non-intentional or routinized practices that exclude coverage (e.g., routines, beats, sourcing patterns). Look for systematic blind spots rather than only overt bias; document institutional practices that produce neglect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsroom decision-making, sociology and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Insights into the newsroom decision-making process and the sociology and structure of newsrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess organizational factors: hierarchies, routines, managerial priorities, economic incentives, and staffing patterns that influence story selection. Examine how structural constraints (e.g., staffing, time, beat assignments) limit coverage of minority communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Power
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze who holds power over news agendas (owners, managers, producers) and how that power shapes what is reported. Consider economic and institutional pressures that determine news priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the extent to which communities and sources of color can gain access to newsrooms, sources, and airtime. Consider barriers to source access, outreach practices, and whether journalists cultivate relationships across diverse communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geography and News
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider spatial factors: which neighborhoods and locales receive coverage, how news geography maps onto racial and socioeconomic demographics, and whether physical or perceived distance affects visibility in news coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: History and News
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how historical context and past relationships between communities and media influence present coverage. Look for patterns rooted in historical marginalization or prior editorial choices that persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible remedies / solutions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and evaluate practical remedies proposed to improve coverage (e.g., newsroom policy changes, outreach strategies, staff diversification, beat realignment). Note reviewers' emphasis that remedies are both ethical and economically sensible. Use these remedies as evaluation criteria for proposed reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology: participant observation / detailed methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix: Detailed Methodology. The study used participant observation and presents qualitative methodology in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When studying newsrooms, apply ethnographic participant-observation techniques: document routines, interactions, and decision-making processes. Use this methodological standard to assess the quality of evidence in similar studies (transparency of methods, depth of access, reflexivity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational and professional relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Required reading for all who are involved in news reporting, mass communication, media and minority studies, and cultural issues in today's society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the book's criteria as curricular or training standards: incorporate its concepts in journalism education, newsroom training, and managerial review. Evaluate whether training materials address the issues Heider raises (incognizant racism, access, decision-making).
